summary: The cardholder starts with no prior balance, makes purchases that push the account above its $1,000 credit limit, and reaches statement close while still over limit. The scenario is designed to test over-limit status at statement close while also representing the modeled grace-period and minimum-payment clauses in the timeline.
assumptions: The account begins a new billing cycle with no previous balance, so the purchase grace-period condition is satisfied.

The issuer allows the purchases to post even though they cause the outstanding balance to exceed the credit limit; this scenario tests the cardholder's over-limit state at statement close rather than transaction denial behavior.
Any over-limit fee described in the agreement is not separately modeled in the IR, so the scenario focuses on the over-limit balance condition at statement close.
The minimum payment obligation arises only after the statement closes and would be due on the later payment due date; no payment is made before statement close in this archetype.

To satisfy the requirement that modeled obligations be represented, the statement-close event is bound to the grace-period clause as the point at which no purchase interest is imposed within at least 25 days, and a later due-check event references the minimum-payment obligation as intentionally unmet in this scenario.
